detailTitle: When to use the registry, carrier or analytics provider

details.title: Free Caller Registry: register the business number
details.what: Free Caller Registry shares registration information with First Orion, Hiya and TNS. Each provider reviews it independently. The registry says a filing gives no guarantee of redress.
details.why: Each confirmation tells you who received the filing and gives you a record to share if you need to escalate.
sources: Free Caller Registry and its terms

details.title: Hiya: register first, then request a review
details.what: Hiya offers free business number registration. Its help page provides a one-time review route for a label that persists after registration.
details.action: Use the business path when the number belongs to your company.
details.why: Hiya also publishes a registration page for Canadian businesses.

details.title: First Orion: use the appeal path for its labels
details.what: First Orion documents business registration and describes how to request remediation for a label you believe is wrong. Its guidance explains why results can differ across carriers.
details.action: Ask which networks your registration covers.
details.why: First Orion explains where it can share your registration. Take a label outside that coverage to the provider that handles it.

details.title: TNS Call Guardian: report a business number
details.what: The TNS feedback form lets a business report that its outgoing number was blocked or mislabeled.
details.why: The form distinguishes between blocking and a label that appears when the call comes through.

details.title: FCC: report a spoofed, blocked or mislabeled number
details.what: The FCC’s complaint guidance covers cases where someone is spoofing your number or where your own number is blocked or marked as possible spam.
details.action: Check your provider’s call records first.
details.why: If people complain about calls you never made, ask the provider to check for spoofing or account misuse. A carrier or analytics ticket can still be necessary for a display issue.

sections.title: Confirm what people see when you call
sections.intro: Make a test call from the actual campaign number to phones you control or have permission to use. Test on more than one receiving network. Record the exact text, date and time.
sections.caption: Three common symptoms and what to check first
rows: Spam warning on one network
Capture the label and use that network’s or analytics provider’s dispute route.
Wrong company name with no spam warning
Ask your phone provider how to correct the displayed business name.
Calls attributed to your number that you did not make
Check call logs and ask your provider to investigate spoofing or account misuse.
copy: Check that callers use the intended business number and that callbacks reach a named person or an identified business voicemail.
Give your provider examples from both affected and unaffected networks. If calls fail to ring, ask it to inspect the call route too.

sections.title: When is paid number reputation monitoring worth it?
sections.intro: Pay for monitoring when you manage enough numbers that checking each one by hand takes too much time.
copy: Ask what networks a paid service covers, how often it checks and what evidence you can export. Branded calling can help identify your business on supported phones. Price monitoring, branding and any dispute help separately.

Review the campaign while the ticket is open. Remove wrong numbers, apply stop requests across lists and give callbacks an owner. Check whether your team is repeatedly contacting people who already gave a clear answer.
If a buyer is screening calls, use our guide to choosing the next call route. If you are buying calling software, ask how a dialer handles caller ID, callbacks, recording and suppression.

faqs.q: Why does my business number show Spam Likely?
faqs.a: Carriers and call protection services can use signals such as call patterns, number history and recipient reports. Confirm which number and receiving network show the warning.

faqs.q: Will Free Caller Registry remove the Spam Likely label?
faqs.a: Registration shares business information with participating services. Each service decides how to use it. Check the affected network again and file a dispute if needed.

faqs.q: How long does a caller ID dispute take?
faqs.a: It varies by provider and case. Keep the ticket number, ask for an expected review date and repeat the same test when you receive a response.

faqs.q: Does correcting the business name remove a spam label?
faqs.a: Displayed name and spam warning are handled separately. Ask your phone provider to fix an incorrect name. Use the relevant label review process for a spam warning.

faqs.q: Should a Canadian business use the same process?
faqs.a: Start with the provider that supplies your number and the carrier where the problem appears. Ask which registry and review route cover your number. Hiya offers Canadian business registration information.
